title: Central Indiana September report (post first)
content:
The September 2026 Central Indiana market report is out. Across the 17-county MIBOR region, the median single-family home sold for $320,000, up 1.3% from last September. There are 7,405 homes on the market, up more than 16% from a year ago, and homes took a median of 27 days to sell, up from 20.

Supply is at 2.9 months, the most balanced the region has been in years. Buyers have real choice and real negotiating room this fall. Sellers can still do well with the right price. Read the full update, or ask us for a free valuation on your home.

title: Marion County / Indianapolis
content:
Indianapolis market update for September 2026: the median home in Marion County sold for $255,000, up 2% from last year. 873 homes sold, and sellers received 98.2% of list price on average.

Inventory is up almost 21% from a year ago, putting supply at 3.5 months, a genuinely balanced market. Buyers can negotiate again. Sellers still sell, but the asking price has to match the market. Our team is based in Southport and works every Indianapolis neighborhood. See the full report for all 17 counties.

title: Johnson County
content:
Johnson County market update for September 2026: the median home sold for $349,900, about flat with last year, across 215 sales. Homes took a median of 32 days to sell, up from 20 a year ago, and inventory is up 18%.

Buyers in Greenwood, Franklin and Bargersville have more options and more time than they've had in years. At 2.6 months of supply, sellers still have an edge, but a longer timeline is worth planning for. Get a free, no-obligation valuation from our Southport office, just north of Greenwood.

title: Hamilton County
content:
Hamilton County market update for September 2026: the median home sold for $487,000, down about 2% from last year, with 475 homes sold. Homes took a median of about 26 days, compared with 16 a year ago.

With just over 1,000 homes on the market and 2.1 months of supply, Carmel, Fishers, Westfield and Noblesville still lean to sellers, but buyers finally have time to compare. Thinking about selling this fall? Request a free home valuation.

title: Hendricks County
content:
Hendricks County market update for September 2026: the median home sold for $370,000, up nearly 6% from last year, one of the strongest price gains in Central Indiana. 217 homes sold.

Inventory is up 16% and homes took a median of 26 days, so buyers in Avon, Brownsburg, Plainfield and Danville have more to choose from. At 2.6 months of supply, sellers keep the advantage. Ask us what your home is worth in today's market.

title: Boone County
content:
Boone County market update for September 2026: the median home sold for $404,949, up about 1.4% from last year, and sales rose more than 50% over last September, 128 homes compared with 85.

At 2.0 months of supply, Zionsville, Whitestown and Lebanon are the tightest market in the region, and homes sold in a median of 21 days. Buyers should come prepared. Sellers, demand is here. Request a free, no-obligation valuation.

title: Hancock County
content:
Hancock County market update for September 2026: the median home sold for $349,100, with 139 homes sold, up 11% from last year. Homes took a median of about 44 days to sell, compared with 20 a year ago.

Supply sits at 2.7 months, so buyers in Greenfield, McCordsville, Fortville and New Palestine have room to be selective. Sellers, the longer timeline is worth planning for. See the full county report, or ask us for your home's value.

title: Madison County
content:
Madison County market update for September 2026: the median home sold for $218,450, up 27% from last September, the largest year-over-year gain in the region, though an unusually low figure last year and a shift in which homes are selling both play into that.

128 homes sold, inventory is up nearly 32%, and homes took a median of 28 days. Buyers in Anderson, Pendleton and Alexandria have more choice than they have in years. Ask us what your specific home would bring.

title: Morgan County
content:
Morgan County market update for September 2026: the median home sold for $285,000, and 72 homes sold, matching last September. Homes sold faster than a year ago, a median of 18 days versus 27, one of the quickest paces in the region.

Supply is at 3.1 months. Well-priced homes in Mooresville, Martinsville and Monrovia are still moving quickly. Considering a move? Request a free home valuation.

title: Shelby County
content:
Shelby County market update for September 2026: the median home sold for $230,000 across 48 sales, and sellers received 98.1% of list price, better than last year.

Inventory is up 22% and homes took a median of about 30 days, so buyers in Shelbyville, Morristown and Fairland have more to consider. Supply is at 2.6 months. Realistic pricing is what's working here. Ask us for a free valuation before you list.

title: Bartholomew County
content:
Bartholomew County market update for September 2026: the median home sold for $295,000, up more than 5% from last year, and sellers received 98.8% of list price, among the strongest in the region.

81 homes sold, homes took a median of 32 days, and supply has risen to 3.1 months, so the market around Columbus is close to balanced. Buyers have room; sellers who present well still get near asking. Request a free home valuation.

title: Jackson County
content:
Jackson County market update for September 2026: homes sold faster here than anywhere else in the region, a median of about 14 days compared with 28 last September. The median sale price came in at $215,000 across 31 sales, a small enough number that the median moves around.

Inventory is up 31% and supply is at 4.0 months, a balanced market. Around Seymour and Brownstown, priced right still means sold quickly. See the full county report.

title: Putnam County
content:
Putnam County market update for September 2026: the median home sold for $300,000, up about 5% from last year, and sales rose more than 50%, 45 homes compared with 29 last September.

Homes took a median of 26 days and supply is at 2.7 months. Buying or selling around Greencastle or Cloverdale? We'll pull real recent sales for your street rather than a county average.

title: Decatur County
content:
Decatur County market update for September 2026: the median home sold for $247,000, about flat with last year, across 26 sales. Homes took a median of 60 days to sell, compared with 23 last September.

Supply is still reasonable at 2.3 months, so the slower pace is mostly about pricing catching up with the market. Buyers around Greensburg and Westport have time to look. Sellers, ask us for a free valuation before you set a price.

title: Montgomery County
content:
Montgomery County market update for September 2026: the median home sold for $200,000 across 39 sales. Homes took a median of 39 days, up from 16 a year ago, though supply remains tight at 2.0 months.

In a market this size, one slow month doesn't make a trend. If you're buying or selling in Crawfordsville, we'll show you what's actually happening on your street. Request a free, no-obligation valuation.

title: Brown County
content:
Brown County market update for September 2026: only 13 homes sold, so the $412,000 median reflects which homes closed more than the market as a whole.

The number that matters is supply: 100 homes on the market and 7.7 months of inventory, the most buyer-friendly market in our area by a wide margin. Homes took a median of 46 days. If you're looking around Nashville, this is the strongest negotiating position buyers have had here in years.

title: Jennings County
content:
Jennings County market update for September 2026: 15 homes sold at a median of $233,500. With volume that low the median swings, so it isn't a trend on its own.

Homes sold slightly faster than last September, a median of 33 days, and there are 45 homes on the market, fewer than a year ago, with supply near 3.0 months. Around North Vernon, be ready to move when the right home appears. Ask us what your home would bring today.

title: Parke County
content:
Parke County market update for September 2026: only 4 homes sold, so the $169,900 median is a small-sample figure rather than a trend.

What's meaningful is inventory: 53 homes on the market, which at the current pace is more than a year's supply. Buyers around Rockville and covered-bridge country have more negotiating room than anywhere else nearby, and sellers need realistic pricing. We'll pull real comparable sales for any home you're considering.

title: Buyers angle (fall market)
content:
Buying in Central Indiana this fall? The September numbers are in your favor. There are 7,405 homes on the market, up more than 16% from last year, and homes are taking a median of 27 days to sell instead of 20.

That means time to look, room to negotiate, and sellers who are motivated heading into winter. Supply is at 2.9 months across the 17-county region, the most balanced it has been in years. See how the buying process works, and talk to our team about what you can expect in your price range.
